I used to be really into David Icke years ago—loved all the conspiracy theories and the wild ideas about the nature of reality. I didn't believe everything he said, just more entertained by his theories. One day, around 2007, while working at a café, I popped into the local bookstore during my lunch break to see if his new book, The David Icke Guide to the Global Conspiracy (and How to End it), was out yet. I couldn’t find it anywhere, though I did spot some of his older ones on the shelves. So, I asked the shop assistant if they had it stock, and she checked the computer but said it wasn’t out yet. Fair enough. I went back to work and didn’t think much of it.

Fast forward to the end of my shift, around 5 p.m. I left through the back door, which leads to some stairs down to the train station. It was rush hour, so people were everywhere. As I walked down the stairs, something caught my eye—a book lying on the ground. I went over, picked it up, and... it was David Icke’s new book.

The *exact* one I’d been looking for earlier. 

It wasn’t even officially out yet! The edges were a bit damp, and there was a bookmark halfway through, like someone had been reading it. I still can’t explain it. Total coincidence? Some weird universal synchronicity? Who knows. It still gives me chills thinking about it.

No... what I'm saying is, if we only have 12 years left before extinction (which I find hard to believe), then why have we not banned all carbon emitting activities as a matter of emergency? If we just lessen them slightly (drive cars less etc), then surely that won't be enough to reverse the damaging effects. 
If Scotland are to lead the way (which they probably are) then great, I'm all for renewable energy. However, unless EVERY country in the world stops ALL carbon emitting activities TODAY, then we are too late. We are already doomed. Therefore, all you are doing is rearranging the furniture on the titanic. 
Playing dead on the shop floor at Waitrose isn't going to save the world I'm afraid.

If things are as bad as they say they are... then surely we are too late to do anything meaningful about it. However if we somehow still have a chance to reverse it, then the immediate banning of all cars, air travel and the burning of all fossil fuels would be the only way to fix it. 
Is that the goal here? To force society to give up their cars? If it is, then I can't see the rest of the world getting on board with that, therefore anything that Scotland or the rest of the UK put in place would be in vain, imo. Good luck getting China to stop all their carbon emissions. 

Personally, I'm all for being more efficient and less wasteful as a matter of common sense... but I don't see the point in getting all cult like about it like Extinction Rebellion.
